# Implement data retention and deletion controls

[Overview](#overview) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Steps](#steps-at-a-glance)

## Overview

When data stores or contractual duties need a controlled retention and disposal schedule. An approved retention schedule with tested deletion, legal-hold handling and evidence of authorized disposal.

Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.

> This is an operational coordination guide. Confirm the applicable company facts, contracts and jurisdictions before acting. Qualified advisers own legal, tax, safety or regulatory determinations and any required professional work. The cited authorities describe their named jurisdictions or frameworks; their rules are not asserted for other countries. External actions require approval for the specific action.

## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Inventory data categories and copies

agent-runnable


Map production systems, document stores, exports, logs and backups to owners and purposes. Identify third-party copies and distinguish records the company controls from data held under customer instructions.

- Sources: [GOV.UK data protection and your business](https://www.gov.uk/data-protection-your-business) · [IRS recordkeeping](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/recordkeeping)

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Approve retention periods and exceptions

human · human approval required


Legal, privacy and business owners determine applicable duties, customer terms and defensible operational needs. Record legal holds and unresolved requirements instead of assigning a single retention period to all data.

- Sources: [GOV.UK data protection and your business](https://www.gov.uk/data-protection-your-business) · [IRS recordkeeping](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/recordkeeping)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Configure the approved lifecycle rules

manual form/portal · human approval required · hard to undo


Authorized administrators implement access, expiration and deletion settings with documented exceptions. Confirm backup and vendor constraints and avoid deleting records subject to a hold or required retention.

- Sources: [GOV.UK data protection and your business](https://www.gov.uk/data-protection-your-business) · [IRS recordkeeping](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/recordkeeping)

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Test deletion and restoration edge cases

agent-runnable


Verify representative data expires or is deleted as intended, including exports and supplier instructions. Check whether restored backups reintroduce deleted information and define the reconciliation process.

- Sources: [GOV.UK data protection and your business](https://www.gov.uk/data-protection-your-business) · [IRS recordkeeping](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/recordkeeping)

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Review disposal evidence and exceptions

human · human approval required


Approve and retain the permitted disposal evidence without recreating the deleted personal data. Monitor failures, holds and changed purposes and reassess the schedule with the relevant owners.

- Verify: An approved retention schedule with tested deletion, legal-hold handling and evidence of authorized disposal.
- Sources: [GOV.UK data protection and your business](https://www.gov.uk/data-protection-your-business) · [IRS recordkeeping](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/recordkeeping)
